reason: Attacked on the edition year and it held, but only just: the year is load-bearing. Two Jowett renderings of Apology 38a circulate. The Internet Classics Archive Jowett reads and that the life which is unexamined is not worth living, which would NOT yield this quotation. The 1892 third edition reads and that the unexamined life is not worth living, which does. I confirmed the 1892 reading in two independent scans of The Dialogues of Plato, in five volumes, vol. II, Jowett, 1892 (Internet Archive cu31924092280134 and dialoguesofplato02plat_2; both title pages give Master of Balliol, Regius Professor of Greek, IN FIVE VOLUMES: VOL. II, 1892, copyright 1892 by Macmillan and Co.), and in Gutenberg ebook 1656, translator credited Benjamin Jowett, which reads word for word: and if I say again that daily to discourse about virtue, and of those other things about which you hear me examining myself and others, is the greatest good of man, and that the unexamined life is not worth living, you are still less likely to believe me. Locator confirmed: the marginal Stephanus number 38 sits at that exact line in the cu31924092280134 scan. Attribution follows the misattribution list's own direction for this line: cite Plato, not Socrates, and name the translator; the speaker Socrates is named in parentheses after the locator, as the rule requires. Source line is 61 characters, leads with the author, has no dash, no straight quote, and the quotation ends in a full stop. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Plato at 0 of 3, not banned. Two flaws found, neither fatal and neither in the shipped fields. First, the evidence block says the clause stands lowercase between two commas; in the 1892 text it is preceded by and that, not by a comma, so only the following comma is there. Second, the evidence block calls the 1892 imprint Oxford University Press; the volumes I opened are the Macmillan 1892 printing, and the British third edition is Clarendon Press. The shipped source line says only trans. Benjamin Jowett, 1892, which is correct either way. One editorial gap worth the editor's eye rather than a refutation: the quotation supplies a capital T and a final full stop at a cut from a lowercase clause, and the note is empty. March precedent (03-cfl-06 on its supplied capital H, 03-poet-01 on its supplied full stop) put that fact in the note. A note here would also earn its keep by saying that earlier Jowett reads the life which is unexamined, so the 1892 in the source is not decoration.
